doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Music's power to change hearts; Pete Seeger and Odetta
summary: Pete Seeger and Odetta taught her that music can change hearts, so she is mindful of her messages.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Speaking of that if you watch the morning news daily do you wonder about the state of human nature in the last five or six, seven years?

I do. Especially having a child in this world too. Yeah I do. And I try to remember what my place is through music and what I can do to do my part in keeping — if anything, keeping spirits up, keeping spirits on the up. That’s important for me. Yeah. It’s been interesting watching this as a humankind and how we’re treating each other. But I think it was Pete Seeger that really opened my eyes to, it was Pete and Odetta — I had a chance to sit with both of them at different times — that reminded me that we have — our work is in our music. And they reminded me that what we do and what we say really matters, and what we sing even more and that music can change hearts, music can change minds, music can change lives, and always remember that. And I try to remember that when I record too. I try to be very mindful of what I’m putting down, what I’m recording. It’s very important to me to put my messages — not necessarily be positive all of them, because I want people to know that I’m a human being. I’ve been up and I’ve had some serious trials, still do. And they’ll keep coming. But my music is my way of working through that and hopefully people can use my music for that too, in their own trials and triumphs.
